item.title: Why my loaf came out flat (and how I fixed it)
item.description: Three flat loaves in a row in October. Here is what it was, in the order I checked. The starter was not strong enough A starter that does not double within 6 hours of a feed is too weak to raise a loaf. Mine had slowed down because the kitchen got colder. Two feeds a day for three days, kept somewhere warm (the oven with only the light on), brought it back.

item.title: My weekday sourdough schedule
item.description: I work office hours, so my bread has to fit around them. This is the schedule I have used for a year, for one loaf with 500 g of flour. The night before At 10 pm I feed the starter: 20 g starter, 50 g flour, 50 g water. It sits on the counter overnight at about 22 °C. Day one Time Step 7:00 am Mix 500 g flour with 350 g water and leave it (autolyse) 7:45 am Add 100 g starter and 10 g salt, squeeze it in 8:00 am One set of stretch and folds, then off to work 6:00 pm Bulk is done when the dough has grown about 50% and jiggles 6:30 pm Shape, put it in a floured banneton, cover, into the fridge Day two Straight from the fridge, any time between 7 am and 7 pm.

item.title: Making a sourdough starter from scratch
item.description: All you need is flour, water and a jar. Rye or whole wheat flour gets going faster than white flour. Days 1 to 3 Mix 50 g whole wheat flour with 50 g water in a jar, cover loosely, and leave it at room temperature. Every 24 hours, throw away all but 50 g and feed it 50 g flour and 50 g water. Days 4 to 7 Switch to feeding every 12 hours.
